source.title: Information-Theoretic Progress Measures reveal Grokking is an Emergent Phase Transition
source.authors: Kenzo Clauw; S. Stramaglia; D. Marinazzo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking and its progress measures on modular addition, using O-Information and synergistic-subnetwork analyses rather than the original studies' measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own modular-addition accuracy curves, O-Information progress measures, and isolated-subnetwork evaluations. Values available only in plots are recorded as figure only. Statements about prior work are not rows. The paper mentions other benchmarks as future work, not as experiments.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own modular-addition grokking curves (2-layer MLP, p=97, 40% data). It tracks O-Information synergy and redundancy as progress measures that, it says, anticipate grokking. It varies weight decay and initialization scale. This is a different method aimed at V1, V2, V3 and V5. Data size, LLMs, cross-run algorithms and optimizer artifacts are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that synergy and redundancy reveal phases before grokking: feature learning, emergence and decoupling, plus divergence and delayed emergence at low weight decay. They say early synergy peaks may predict grokking, and that weight decay and high initialization enhance the emergent phase and shrink the gap. They attribute grokking to an emergent phase transition and suggest it may stem from improper hyperparameter tuning. They call the causal-subnetwork evidence and the predictive claim preliminary, needing more models and statistical tests.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 2-layer ReLU fully connected network on modular addition, with 40% of the data and AdamW; differs by analyzing O-Information-derived synergy/redundancy and synergistic subnetworks, and by varying weight decay and initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported grokking and synergy outcomes vary with weight decay (0.1, 2.0, 10, 50) and initialization factor (1, 8, 50).
record.problems: The experiments use a simple modular-addition benchmark and a 2-layer network; the paper itself calls the subnetwork-causality findings preliminary. It reports five random seeds per experiment but does not state how the plotted curves aggregate them. Accuracy and progress-measure values are presented in plots without exact numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The feature binning and clustering may not capture the full feature structure, as the authors note.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only 40% is used).

Identification of a specific (e.g. Fourier) algorithm, and direct evidence that memorizing components are removed. The 'decoupling/compression' phase is only an interpretation of synergy and redundancy trends.
Non-algorithmic data (images, text, molecules), and any explicit lazy-to-rich transition.
Entire version: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Circuit efficiency comparison, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Entire version. The authors only note that AdamW's internal regularization may influence results.

missing.what: Alpha=8 synergistic-subnetwork result: the subnetwork has a similar grokking period to the original model.
Section 4 states the low weight decay as 0.01, contradicting 0.1 elsewhere; the row condition should note the ambiguity.
Alpha=8 run: an early rapid drop in redundancy followed by a delayed rapid rise in synergy, which the authors frame as an emergent phase.

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is figure-only, with five seeds and no stated aggregation or uncertainty. The text has several typos and broken references: weight decay 0.01 vs 0.1, 'alpha too high (5)', a missing Figure 10, and Figure 7's caption duplicating Figure 6's. Failure-to-grok rows were unlinked from V1 because V1 makes no claim for every hyperparameter. No-grok runs were re-read as consistent with V2's predictive progress-measure claim.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests delayed generalization on modular addition, but does not vary training-set size; it therefore does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
It measures synergy, redundancy, and synergistic subnetworks, but does not identify a Fourier algorithm or directly track removal of memorizing components.
It varies weight decay and initialization on modular addition only. It does not test non-algorithmic data, weight-norm control as such, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
It tests how weight decay relates to grokking, but does not establish that low norm selects a more efficient circuit, nor test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
It does not identify and compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts against controlled alternatives.
